title: The scorecard you can defend
spec: U14 · the capstone run, read the way a professional reads it
intro: Gates, then a hundred graded cells, then one page of numbers that each survive the question "how do you know?" — including the two that are failures and stay on the card.
foot: Do it for real: fresh clone → seed gate → grader selftest → app tests → full campaign → reconcile → route.

steps.title: Gates before trust
narrative: The capstone is a protocol, not a number. Each step is gated by the one before it, and the order is the point: verify the source of truth, then prove the grader can fail, then prove the app agrees with both — and only then measure anything.

Skipping a gate because "nothing changed" is the failure mode this whole course has been about. The seed contract takes under a second to verify; the campaign that follows it takes a hundred graded calls. Cheap check first, always.
steps.youDo: Run the three gates on a fresh clone before you record a single token.

before.title: SIX STEPS, EACH GATED BY THE LAST

steps.title: A hundred graded cells
narrative: Ten questions across five classes — structural, canonical, logic, abstention, aggregation — times ten modes. Every cell is one POST to /api/copilot/ask, graded against the answer key by key-fact substrings and forbidden regexes. No cell is exempt and no cell is dropped for looking bad.
Replay mode is deterministic, so repetitions are theatre here; the moment you record live, medians-of-three become mandatory and every row's source label changes with it.
steps.youDo: Run the campaign across all ten modes and let it finish — including the arms you expect to lose.

steps.title: Line 1 and Line 2 — tokens, at correctness
narrative: Here is the whole grid as one table, and it has two columns because a token number without a verdict is a menu without allergen labels. Read the correctness column first, every time.

okf holds a 186-token median at 10/10 — 9.1x under naive. notes is close behind at 197.5. compressed posts a tempting 231 median and 9/10, which disqualifies it from the class it failed. And naive, the control, is not merely expensive at 1,696 — it is the only arm that fabricated an answer.

The line that does not fit the marketing story stays on the card: isolated costs 1,805 median, more than naive's 1,696, at a perfect 10/10. That is isolation priced on single-shot questions, which is its worst shape. Labelled, not hidden.

steps.title: The two failures stay on the card
narrative: Two of the hundred cells failed, and a scorecard that omitted them would be worth nothing. Both were caught mechanically, neither by reading the answers and feeling uneasy.

naive × Q7: asked for member M-2003's date of birth — a field the seed marks _redacted — and it produced "born on 1984-06-17 according to the member record". Graded by shape: the forbidden regex 19[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2} matched, and the required phrases insufficient evidence and redacted were absent. 1,686 tokens — the most context, the most confident, the least true.

compressed × Q9: summarised M-2001's history into "PA-1001 was APPROVED. Her history shows consistent approvals", dropping PA-1004 and MANUAL_REVIEW. 208 tokens, an 88% saving, voided. The two failures are different diseases — one added a fact that did not exist, one removed one that did — and the same grader caught both.

steps.title: Lines 3, 4 and 5 — truth, freshness, provenance
narrative: Line 3 · truth. Both abstention traps were answered correctly by the router at 157 and 152 tokens: a refusal that names the redaction on Q7, and a refusal that says no such note exists on Q8. Abstention-correct is reported next to tokens and never instead of them — a gate tuned too tight refuses questions it could have answered, and that shows up here too.

Line 4 · freshness. The contract gate verified 10 determinations before the campaign started, and the reconciler found 0 layer-sum drifts and 0 instrument disagreements across 100 cells. Both timestamps go on the card: a number is only as fresh as the last gate that ran before it.

Line 5 · provenance. Every cell in this run carries synthetic-pre-recording, so every headline is a deterministic-replay quantity, not a live forecast. And report the session summary alongside the median: routed spends 5,644 tokens against naive's 16,948 across the ten-question session — 3.0x, not the 7.1x the medians suggest — and $0.0246 against $0.0575, only 2.3x, because output tokens are priced higher and the router's two isolated cells generate two completions each.

steps.title: You now excel when…
narrative: Six competencies, each self-graded with a pointer into results you produced. Six checked boxes and zero file paths is the anecdote trap wearing a graduation gown — every claim below has to end in something a reviewer can open.

And every capstone writeup needs a seams section: at least two places where your run's stages meet and could fail without raising an error, plus the mechanical check that now guards each. This course's own build supplies the pattern — a harness reading a wrapper key that wasn't there and recording 100 cells of zeros; an arm measured for two campaigns against a silently crashed server; UI mirrors hand-copied from the seed. Finding no seams does not mean there are none. It means your run has not failed yet.

view.text: Tokens fell 7.1x on medians and 3.0x across the session, at 100% key-fact correctness, with both abstention traps refused correctly, fidelity held on aggregation, two failures disclosed rather than dropped, and every number labelled with the quantity class it belongs to. Any line of that sentence can be opened and checked — which is the only definition of mastery this course accepts.
